summary: The exact reduction, carry profile, Weil/lift bound and prime-conductor primary congruence all check out; I re-derived B, the lift condition, e_t+e_(-t)=2, the lambda^2 congruence, and brute-forced #surface = p^2+p+1+C for (p,d)=(7,3),(13,3),(13,4),(11,5). The artifact confirms 14 controls, 1032 triple records, 64/64 balanced LLL rows, 246 phase checks, 51 profiles and 200 symmetric triples at p=2^61-1, d=11 with |C|<=Bp. The only problem is scope: the opening 'superseding' paragraph states that the prime-conductor asymptotic quantum opening is removed without saying, there, that this rests on a review-pending local application of an unimplemented imported algorithm (conceded only in the closing section). Composite conductors remain open, as the note says.

claims.quote: Under the stated Jacobi/primary identities this removes the prime-conductor asymptotic quantum opening
claims.finding: Headline drops a condition stated elsewhere: the removal rests on JACOBI_KNOWN_NORM_REDUCTION, whose local application of Lenstra-Silverberg Theorem 1.3 is review pending and whose recovery algorithm is not executed; the closing section concedes 'Independent review of the local application is still needed', but the superseding sentence presents the removal as established.

claims.quote: The number of terms is B=(d-1)(d^2-3d+3), and each has absolute value p
claims.finding: Admissible triples = (d-1)^3 - (d-1)(d-2) = (d-1)(d^2-3d+3); three nontrivial characters with nontrivial product give |J|=p, including the a+b=0 case where J=p*chi^a(-1). Brute force at four small (p,d) reproduces #surface=p^2+p+1+C.

claims.quote: If p>2B, C mod p^2 has a unique lift in [-Bp,Bp]
claims.finding: The 2Bp+1 integers in [-Bp,Bp] are distinct mod p^2 when p>=2B+1. At the large control C=376191977256968888606 is well within 910p.

claims.quote: It satisfies e_t+e_(-t)=2 and sum e_t=phi(d)
claims.finding: With S_t the residue sum, S_(-t)=3d-S_t and a+b+c nonzero mod d give floor(S_(-t)/d)=2-floor(S_t/d), so e_t+e_(-t)=2; summing over the phi(d)/2 pairs gives phi(d).

claims.quote: For odd prime conductor ell, lambda=1-zeta_ell, the THREE-character sum obeys
claims.step: Prime Conductors Need No Phase Oracle
claims.finding: Re-derived: there are p^2-3p+3 = 1 mod ell nonzero triples, and the linear coefficient is (p-2)*sum log_chi(x), divisible by ell for odd ell. The test A(1)=1, A'(1)=0 mod ell is independent of the representative because Phi_ell(1) and Phi_ell'(1) are both 0 mod ell, and the 2ell roots +/-zeta^k have distinct residues mod lambda^2.

claims.quote: LLL plus primary normalization reproduces all six prime-conductor native surface controls
claims.finding: The artifact shows CLASSICAL_PUBLIC_IDEAL_RECONSTRUCTION_COMPLETED for the d=3,5,7 controls (six) and for the p=2^61-1, d=11 control with 51 profiles, 200 triples and point count 5316911983139663865501362488876572959; all 64 small LLL attempts report a balanced generator. The note correctly scopes this as finite success with no worst-case LLL theorem.

summary: The reduction to Lenstra-Silverberg Theorem 1.3 appears correct: I checked the theorem statement (CM-order, fractional ideal, totally positive w with I*bar(I)=Aw, deterministic polynomial-time decision and recovery). The local steps hold: I*bar(I)=p^2 A from e_t+e_(-t)=2, the unit ratio being a root of unity, the trace-Gram output-size bound, and the group-ring lift with zero augmentation and index p^ell. The artifact matches six small controls and 51 large profiles with recovery not executed and review not completed. The title states the removal as settled, although the note itself says the local application is review pending and the recovery algorithm was not run.

claims.quote: Known Relative Norm Removes The Prime-Conductor Quantum Opening
claims.finding: The title presents the conclusion unconditionally. The status line and the next-action section make it 'subject to independent review of the application', and the Lenstra-Silverberg recovery was not executed (artifact: classical_known_norm_recovery_executed=false, independent_or_formal_review_completed=false). Polynomial succinct-input time also needs the ell=poly(log p) promise stated only in the body.

claims.quote: Theorem 1.3, gives a deterministic classical polynomial-time decision AND recovery algorithm
claims.finding: The arXiv v3 statement of Theorem 1.3 matches: given a CM-order A, a fractional ideal I and a totally positive w with I*bar(I)=Aw, it decides whether some v has I=Av and v*bar(v)=w, and computes v if so; no GRH is stated.

claims.quote: Since e_t+e_(-t)=2, we have I*bar(I)=product_t P_t^2=p^2*A
claims.finding: Conjugation maps P_t to P_(-t), so I*bar(I)=prod P_t^(e_t+e_(-t)), and p splits completely as prod_t P_t because ell|(p-1).

claims.quote: implies ell*sum a_j^2-(sum a_j)^2=(ell-1)*p^2
claims.finding: Tr(J*bar(J)) in the power basis has Gram ell*I-11^T, with eigenvalues ell and 1, and the trace equals (ell-1)p^2. Hence |a_j|<=sqrt(ell-1)*p.

claims.quote: Its augmentation is0, hence that multiple is0
claims.finding: In Z[X]/(X^ell-1), Phi_ell*h = h(1)*Phi_ell, whose augmentation is ell*h(1). Since v(1)=p gives zero augmentation, h(1)=0. The index p^(phi(ell)+1)=p^ell equals |v(1)*N(J)|=p*p^(ell-1), which proves equality.

claims.quote: For odd prime ell the root group is {+/-zeta^k}
claims.finding: The ratio v/J is a relative-norm-1 unit of a CM field, so it is a root of unity by Kronecker. The 2ell roots are separated by the lambda^2 primary test shown in the surface note.

summary: The load-bearing algebra checks. A^3=(sum c_j^3)I follows from uniform omega-commutation, and the artifact records 503 for c=[2,3,5,7]. The Hermitian completion has no uniform last vertex for m>=2, and the recorded determinant -4200-8400*omega has nonzero norm. The source-as-solution identity holds: X-pivot labels make <0|W|0>=Tr(W)/3^m for every element of the generated group, so pilot and output energies agree. I checked that the readout's quadratic reordering phase cancels against z.x, which gives the stated m(m-1)/2+2m gate count (artifact: 5 and 9) and the 3D-bond output MPS formula. Claims are scoped to energy estimation and to finite witnesses, without asymptotic rank or hardness inference.

claims.quote: the one-directional relation gives A^3=(sum c_j^3)I
claims.finding: U_j^3=I, and every ordered pair omega-commutes in a fixed direction, so the q-multinomial coefficients [3]_omega vanish. The artifact's A_cubed_scalar is 503=8+27+125+343.

claims.quote: no generator is uniform against all remaining predecessors
claims.finding: Each U_j commutes with its partner U_j^dagger but omega-commutes with every U_k for k != j, so with m>=2 no generator can be placed last.

claims.quote: has a4x4 minor with EXACT determinant -4200-8400*omega, nonzero in Z[omega]
claims.finding: N(a+b*omega)=a^2-ab+b^2=52,920,000 != 0, matching the artifact. This gives rank>=4>3=degree+1 at that single cut, which is all the note claims.

claims.quote: Thus for ANY normalized pilot, input and output have identical energy expectations
claims.finding: Since E_r|0>=|r>, the pilot is M|0> for M=sum alpha_r E_r, and the output energy is Tr(M^dagger H M)/Tr(M^dagger M). Each group element whose X-label is zero is the identity (z is determined by x), so <0|W|0>=Tr(W)/3^m and the two expectations coincide. The native controls agree to about 1e-15.

claims.quote: It uses m(m-1)/2+2m ideal logical qutrit Clifford gates
claims.finding: z labels take m(m-1)/2 SUMs, plus m Fourier and m SUM gates. The reordering phase omega^(-sum_{j<k} r_j r_k) cancels against omega^(z.x), so no extra phase gates are needed. The artifact records 5 gates for m=2 and 9 for m=3.

claims.quote: bond controlled-precision pilot cannot support an ENERGY-estimation separation here
claims.finding: Follows from the intertwiner identity plus a classical MPO contraction. The premises (constructible, controlled precision, MPS) and the restriction to energy estimation are stated, and the 64-site control is explicitly labelled a product-pilot calibration.

summary: The radius recurrence is correct. Independence makes every P_j*(product of predecessors) a traceless Pauli, giving balanced sign sectors in the commuting case; an all-anticommuting Q exists, giving a symmetric spectrum; and anticommuting additions satisfy H_j^2=H_(j-1)^2+c_j^2 I. The explicit ground-state rotation angle -atan2(c,R) checks against the 2x2 block [[-R,c],[c,R]]. The outward-rounding width bound holds because endpoint widths stay grid multiples; the 512-term certificate has width 330*2^-80 with 341 root steps, and the native controls match dense eigenvalues. The ZZI+IZZ+ZIZ counterexample (ground -1) is correct, and the falsifier is scoped to ground energy only.

claims.quote: Each eigenspace of H_(j-1) therefore has equal +1/-1 multiplicities for P_j
claims.finding: f(H_(j-1)) is a combination of subset products of earlier labels. Independence makes P_j times any such product a non-identity Pauli, hence traceless, and commuting P_j restricts to a traceless involution on each eigenspace.

claims.quote: Thus every H_j has a spectrum symmetric about zero
claims.finding: Independent labels make the symplectic system full row rank, so Q with Q P_i Q=-P_i exists and Q H Q=-H.

claims.quote: R_j = sqrt(R_(j-1)^2 + c_j^2)
claims.finding: Anticommutation with all predecessors cancels the cross terms, so H_j^2=H_(j-1)^2+c_j^2 I. Recomputed on the controls: XIII/ZXII/IIXI/ZZZX gives 2.19637, matching the dense eigenvalue -2.196370942790219.

claims.quote: so interval width is at most (number of root steps)*2^(-b)
claims.finding: Each root step is 1-Lipschitz. Commuting additions shift both endpoints equally, so the width stays a multiple of 2^-b and each floor/ceil adds at most one grid step. Artifact: 512-term width 165/2^79=330*2^-80 <= 341 root steps.

claims.quote: applies exp(-i theta Z_<j Y_j/2), theta=-atan2(c_j,R_(j-1))
claims.finding: Z_<j anticommutes with every earlier canonical word, so {|g,0>, Z_<j|g>|1>} spans an invariant block [[-R,c],[c,R]]. The rotation gives cos(theta/2)|g,0>+sin(theta/2)Z_<j|g>|1>, with tan(theta/2)=-c/(R+sqrt(R^2+c^2)): the lower eigenvector.

claims.quote: Dependence matters: ZZI+IZZ+ZIZ has ground energy-1, not-3
claims.finding: The product of the three signs is a square, so not all three terms can be -1; the minimum is -1, and the labels sum to zero.

summary: The derivations hold: e3=e1*e2 over F2, exact balance, the RM(3,d) first-moment flat bound (tight at t=3, N=1, where it gives 1/2), the third-difference flat construction, the scoped IID suffix tail bound, and R/2-R^2/4>R^2/4 for 0<R<1. The live table matches the artifact (best scores 7,7/27,27/30,30/105,104; 50 and 11 forced predicates; 512 and 32768 residual messages), and I recomputed the DQI means 0.688982, 0.747358 and 0.816830. The weakness is the title: 'A Structural Classical Falsifier' presents the attack as a falsifier, while the note's own asymptotic section says this attack, under its IID premise, cannot reach the DQI target and that the finite win does not prove dequantization.

claims.quote: Explicit Cubic-Target OPI: A Structural Classical Falsifier
claims.finding: The headline drops the scope stated in the body: the falsification is a finite, seeded, best-of-four score comparison at four sizes, with no matched tails or runtime. The note's conditional asymptotic analysis says that if E/N->R this attack cannot beat (1+R)/2, below the DQI target 1/2+sqrt(R/2(1-R/2)), so the title should not read as a falsifier of the asymptotic target.

claims.quote: Dense symmetric cubics are not an escape: e3=e1*e2 in the Boolean ring
claims.finding: In e1*e2, pairs are counted twice (0 mod 2) and triples three times (1 mod 2), giving e3.

claims.step: Why The Quadratic Rank Argument Does Not Automatically Transfer
claims.finding: An accepted flat cannot contain the z0 direction, so it is a graph over a base d-flat: there are 2^(t-1-d)[t-1 choose d]_2 base flats and 2^(d+1) affine heights, each matched with probability 2^-D3(d). Artifact: t=3, d=2, N=1 gives 1/2, and t=63, d=20 gives an exponent of about -439, consistent.

claims.quote: Pr(best pool score >= k) <= min(1, S * Pr(Binomial(N-E,1/2) >= k-E))
claims.step: Why This Does Not Settle The Asymptotic Question
claims.finding: Uniform independent suffix constants make each fixed message's suffix acceptance IID Bernoulli(1/2), and the union bound over a prefix-determined pool gives the bound. The artifact applies it (e.g. N=127: E=51, S=2048, k=104, union upper about 0.78, nonvacuous but weak) and labels it an IID-model statement only.

claims.quote: since R/2-R^2/4 > R^2/4
claims.step: Why This Does Not Settle The Asymptotic Question
claims.finding: 1/2+sqrt(R/2-R^2/4) > (1+R)/2 is equivalent to R/2 > R^2/2, i.e. R<1.

claims.quote: There is no finite best-score advantage in these comparisons
claims.finding: Best classical scores (7/7, 27/31, 30/31, 105/127 and 104/127) exceed the recomputed filter means 0.688982, 0.747358 and 0.816830 at every size. The artifact confirms 32 attempts, all EXACT_RESIDUAL_AFFINE_OPTIMUM, below cap 18. The mismatch between best-of-four and a mean is conceded.
